concepts.name: Electric Charge & Quantization
concepts.description: Fundamental property of matter causing electric force. Protons (+e) and electrons (-e). Charge is quantized (Q = ne) and conserved.

concepts.name: Electric Current & Drift
concepts.description: Rate of flow of electric charges through a conductor per unit time. Conventional current flows from positive to negative terminal; electrons flow opposite. Measured by Ammeter in series.

concepts.name: Electric Potential & Potential Difference
concepts.description: Work done in moving a unit positive charge from one point to another in an electrostatic field. Maintained by a cell/battery. Measured by Voltmeter connected in parallel.

concepts.name: Circuit Diagrams & Symbols
concepts.description: Schematic representation of an electric circuit using standardized symbols for cells, switches, resistors, variable resistors (rheostats), ammeters, and voltmeters.

concepts.name: Ohm's Law & Resistance
concepts.description: At constant temperature, current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to potential difference across its ends (V ∝ I, V = IR). Resistance is the opposition to current.

concepts.name: Factors Affecting Resistance & Resistivity
concepts.description: Resistance is directly proportional to length (L) and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area (A): R = ρ(L/A). Resistivity (ρ) is an intrinsic material property independent of dimensions.

concepts.name: Resistors in Series
concepts.description: End-to-end connection of resistors. Current remains constant across all resistors. Total potential difference is the sum of individual drops: V = V1 + V2. Equivalent resistance: Rs = R1 + R2 + ...

concepts.name: Resistors in Parallel
concepts.description: Resistors connected across two common points. Potential difference is identical across all branches. Total current is the sum of branch currents: I = I1 + I2. Equivalent resistance: 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...

concepts.name: Heating Effect of Electric Current (Joule's Law)
concepts.description: Conversion of electric energy into thermal energy when current flows through a resistance. Heat produced is proportional to I^2, R, and t: H = I^2 * R * t. Applied in electric irons, heaters, and fuses.

concepts.name: Electric Power & Commercial Energy
concepts.description: Rate at which electric energy is consumed or dissipated: P = VI = I^2*R = V^2/R. Commercial unit of electric energy is kilowatt-hour (1 kWh = 3.6 × 10^6 J or 1 'unit').
